seo.title: Conscious Coral Reef Restoration Tourism | Oceans Alive Foundation
seo.description: Turning a 30 hectare sanctuary's ecological recovery into a certified, income generating reef tourism enterprise at Kuruwitu, Kenya's first community marine sanctuary.

EXPERIENCE.title: Coral Education
EXPERIENCE.body: Restoration tours explaining how the sanctuary recovered and why it matters.

EXPERIENCE.title: Nursery Work
EXPERIENCE.body: Hands on time in the coral nursery, learning how fragments are grown and cared for.

EXPERIENCE.title: Reef Out-Planting
EXPERIENCE.body: Artificial reef out-planting sessions where visitors help transplant juvenile coral.

EXPERIENCE.title: Plant Your Own Coral
EXPERIENCE.body: A signature moment: every visitor gets to plant a coral of their own on the reef.

PROGRESS: Entrance and reception area cleaned, with new wall paintings of local marine life
Collaboration MOU between Oceans Alive and KCW-CBO revised
Marketing consultant engaged to design a communication strategy
Snorkels, masks and reef shoes procured for tourists

hero.title: Conscious Coral Reef Restoration Tourism
hero.text: Nineteen years of community conservation at Kuruwitu, Kenya's first community marine sanctuary, becoming a certified, income generating coral restoration tourism enterprise.

ecologicalRecoveryDashboard.heading: Nineteen Years of Ecological Recovery, By the Numbers
ecologicalRecoveryDashboard.text5: Kuruwitu is managed by the Kuruwitu Conservation and Welfare CBO and the Kuruwitu Beach Management Unit under traditional law, and now co-managed under Kenya's Fisheries Regulations. The CBO has run its eco tourism venture for over 10 years, becoming a popular destination and a living classroom for other fishing communities. But climate driven coral bleaching, illegal fishing and unregulated tourism now threaten those gains, which is exactly what this programme is built to hold the line against.

thePlan.heading: Three Moves to a Certified Destination
thePlan.text2: Develop a professional business plan and tourism strategy built around the sanctuary's proven ecological recovery.
thePlan.text4: Upgrade facilities and safety compliance, and certify staff to national tourism board standards.
thePlan.text6: Formalize Aquatic Safari packages with the Kenya Association of Tour Operators, who have already expressed interest.

visitorExperience.heading: A Beach to Reef Package, Built Around Participation
visitorExperience.text: Tourists, schools and corporate groups pay to take part in an aquatic safari, not just watch one. The result funds reef restoration, monitoring and community livelihoods while widening every visitor's understanding of what protecting a coral reef actually takes.

lookingAhead.text: Beyond Kuruwitu, the model is designed to travel: a grassroots led, tourism linked, income generating blueprint that other coastal communities across Kenya can adapt for their own reefs.

callToAction.heading: Help Safeguard Kuruwitu's Reefs
callToAction.text: Your support helps finance reef restoration, monitoring and community livelihoods through regenerative tourism.
